page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question
Chemical Equilibrium, Acids and Bases · 2 marks

steps.label: No shift, K unchanged
lines: A catalyst does not change the equilibrium
position and does not change the value of
It increases the forward and the backward
steps.why: The equilibrium position depends on the ratio of the two rates. A catalyst multiplies both rates by the same factor, so the ratio — and with it the position and K — stays the same.
common_mistakes: Writing that a catalyst shifts the equilibrium forward. It shifts nothing.
Writing that a catalyst increases the yield. The amounts at equilibrium are unchanged.
steps.memory_tip: Both rates rise by the same factor, so the equilibrium position does not move.
steps.margin_note: The word equally is the reason — write it.

steps.label: What the catalyst does change
lines: The composition at equilibrium stays the
same; the system only arrives at that

lines.text: A catalyst only reduces the time needed to reach equilibrium

steps.why: This is the one real effect: with both rates raised, every stage of the approach to equilibrium runs faster, so the same final state is reached in less time.
common_mistakes: Writing that the catalyst is used up. It is recovered unchanged.
Confusing faster arrival with a different destination — the equilibrium mixture is identical.
steps.memory_tip: The same equilibrium mixture is reached, only in less time.
steps.margin_note: Two sentences: what stays the same, and the one thing that changes.

insider_note: The question sounds like one thing but is marked as two: what does not change, and the one thing that does. An answer that only says the equilibrium does not shift scores one of the two marks.
